title: On-call and Incident Response: SOP, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document is the canonical Redwood Inference on-call and incident response playbook. It covers the incident lifecycle, runbook structure and authoring guidelines, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and handoff procedures, game-day planning, and templates for status page and customer communications. Intended audience: on-call engineers, SREs, incident commanders (ICs), engineering managers, and support/CS leads.

1) Goals and scope
- Minimize customer impact and restore service quickly while preserving clear, auditable communications.
- Provide consistent triage, escalation, and remediation steps for common failure modes.
- Ensure learnings are captured and actioned via postmortems and follow-up tasks.
- Maintain safe and testable on-call rotations with clear ownership and SLAs.

2) Incident severity classification (use these tiers for routing and comms)
| Severity | Customer Impact | Example symptoms | Initial target MTTR | Page/Notify |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sev1 / P0 | Major outage: most customers unable to use the product | API returns 5xx, control plane down, models unavailable | 60 minutes | Pager + Slack #incident + Exec notify |
| Sev2 / P1 | Significant partial degradation | Elevated latency, intermittent errors, degraded throughput | 4 hours | Pager for on-call + Slack channel |
| Sev3 / P2 | Minor degradation / feature impairment | Slightly increased latency for non-critical routes | 24 hours | Slack only / ticket |
| Sev4 / P3 | Informational / planned maintenance | Scheduled maintenance, non-urgent updates | N/A | No pager; update status page if customer-facing |

3) Incident lifecycle (quick reference)
1. Detection & Acknowledgement
   - Alert fires (PagerDuty / Opsgenie) or manual detection via dashboards/logs/customer report.
   - On-call engineer acknowledges within configured acknowledgement SLO (Sev1: 5m, Sev2: 15m).
2. Triage
   - Gather impact, scope, affected services, and recent deploys.
   - Assign Incident Commander (IC) if severity >= Sev2.
3. Mitigation & Communication
   - IC declares incident severity and documents mitigation steps in incident channel.
   - Post to Status Page (see templates) for customer-facing incidents (Sev1/Sev2).
4. Resolution
   - Apply fix or rollback; validate with health checks, synthetic tests, and user verification.
5. Recovery & Restore
   - Confirm service health for at least 30 minutes with no regression before declaring resolved.
6. Postmortem & Actions
   - IC or assigned author writes postmortem within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev2. Assign action items and owners.

4) Pager & escalation matrix
- Primary on-call (service owner) -> 15 minutes -> secondary -> 30 minutes -> IC escalation to on-call lead -> 60 minutes -> Eng manager -> Exec
- Pager schedule is maintained in the on-call calendar (Google Calendar + PagerDuty overrides). All engineers with on-call duties must keep rotation availability updated.

5) Runbook authoring template and mandatory sections
- Runbook title (short, dash-case).
- Service and team owner.
- Impact summary (what user-facing symptoms look like).
- Detection & observability (metrics, dashboards, logs, example alert queries).
- Quick triage checklist (1-2 line checks to narrow fault domain).
- Mitigation steps (ordered, tested commands with expected outputs).
- Post-remediation validation steps.
- Rollback steps (explicit commands and safety checks).
- Contacts and escalation (links to on-call schedule, Slack channel).
- Last updated and author.

Example runbook excerpt (GPU service OOM):
- Detection: GPU memory pressure on node group "gpu-serving-pool" with >90% memory usage for 2 consecutive 10s windows; alert: gpu-memory-pressure-high.
- Quick triage: 1) Check recent deploys (last 30m) 2) Check KV cache miss rate 3) Query per-model token length distribution.
- Mitigation (fast path): 1) Disable burst routing to dedicated pool: `rdctl routing set --service inference --policy conservative` 2) Scale up replica set: `k scale deployment model-runtime --replicas=6 -n inference` 3) If memory error persists, evict offending pod: `kubectl delete pod <pod> -n inference`
- Validation: Successful rollout and 95th percentile token latency returns to below SLO within 30m.

6) Postmortem requirement and template
- When required: All Sev1 and Sev2 incidents must have a postmortem. Postmortem must be published in Confluence and linked to the incident ticket.
- Timeline: Initial postmortem draft within 72 hours; final postmortem with action items closed or owner assigned within 14 days.
- Postmortem fields (flat list to copy into Confluence):
  - Title
  - Incident ID / PagerDuty link
  - Severity
  - Incident start/end timestamps
  - Summary (1-2 sentences)
  - Impact (customer count, percent of traffic affected, revenue impact estimate if available)
  - Root cause(s)
  - Timeline (ordered bullets with timestamps)
  - Contributing factors
  - Corrective actions (owner + due date)
  - Preventative measures / follow-ups
  - Lessons learned
  - Status (draft / in_review / closed)

7) On-call rotations and handoffs
- Rotation length: 1 week for primary on-call; 1 week for secondary. Weekend rotations are the same.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed before shift change):
  1. Confirm you reviewed open incidents and active alerts.
  2. Share any ongoing mitigations/follow-ups in the rotation channel.
  3. Confirm access (PagerDuty, GCP/AWS consoles, runbook links).
  4. Update calendar and Slack status to indicate on-call.
- Escalation responsibilities and on-call etiquette: Keep messages concise, include reproducible steps, and avoid making permanent config changes without peer review for non-emergency fixes.

8) Game-day planning and execution
- Purpose: Validate runbooks, train new on-callers, and exercise cross-team coordination under realistic failure scenarios.
- Frequency: Quarterly for platform teams; each service to run at least one game-day per year.
- Roles: Game-day lead, observer(s), incident commander, responder(s), customer comms owner.
- Example scenario: Simulate regional capacity loss: disable traffic to us-west region, verify routing fallback, and validate degraded latency behavior.
- After action: Produce a short AAR (after action report) with failures, time to detect/resolve, and action items.

9) Status page and customer communications templates
- Status page policy: Any customer-facing incident (Sev1/Sev2) must have a status page entry within 30 minutes of incident declaration. Use the status page templates below.

Status page post template (short):
- Title: [Service] degraded / outage - {short description}
- Impact: {summary of affected customers/functionality}
- Current status: Investigating / Partial service restoration / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
- Next update: {ETA or time}
- Details: {bullet list of affected components and brief mitigation steps}

Customer email / CS template (Sev1 initial):
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference - {service} - {short summary}
Hi {Customer Name},
We are investigating an incident affecting {service} that may impact {affected features}. Our on-call team has been alerted and an incident commander is coordinating mitigation. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. You can monitor status at {STATUS_PAGE_URL}.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

Customer update (follow up):
Subject: Update - Incident impacting {service} - {short summary}
Hi {Customer Name},
Update: We have identified the root cause as {root cause summary}. Mitigation steps applied: {list}. Impact: {reduced / resolved / remaining}. Next update: {time or resolution ETA}.

Customer resolution (post-incident):
Subject: Incident resolved - {service} - {summary}
Hi {Customer Name},
The incident affecting {service} has been resolved as of {time}. Root cause: {root cause}. Actions taken: {short list}. We will publish a full postmortem at {CONFLUENCE_LINK}. If you experienced data loss or persistent errors, contact support@redwood.ai.

10) Metrics, dashboards and SLOs to monitor
- Key metrics: 5xx rate, 95th/99th token latency, request throughput (rps), model server CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit ratio, queue length, error budget burn rate.
- Example SLOs (service level objectives):
  - Availability SLO: 99.95% per month for core text generation API (excludes scheduled maintenance).
  - Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency < 250ms on hosted small models.
  - Error budget: 0.05% monthly error budget.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m -> Sev2 alert
  - 5xx rate > 2% for 2m -> Sev1 alert
  - 95th latency increase > 2x baseline for 5m -> Sev2

11) Tooling and playbooks (commands & links)
- PagerDuty: incident creation and runbook links are embedded in every alert.
- Status page: {STATUS_PAGE_URL} (internal template).
- Quick CLI/console commands to check runtime cluster: `k get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=app=model-runtime`
- Example health check curl for API: `curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .`

12) Ownership and governance
- Document owner: eng-sre (contact: eng-sre@redwood.ai).
- Runbook owners: each service must list a primary runbook owner and a secondary. Runbooks reviewed quarterly.
- Incident reviews and postmortem governance: Eng SRE chairs postmortem review meeting for Sev1 incidents. Track action item closure in Jira with label `incident-action`.

Appendices
A) Quick escalation cheat sheet (one line per role)
- Primary on-call: initial triage and mitigation steps.
- Secondary: backup for primary and execution of complex mitigations.
- IC: owns incident coordination, comms, and timeline.
- Eng manager: resource escalation and cross-team coordination.
- CS lead: customer notifications and follow up.

B) Postmortem checklist (before publishing)
- [ ] Timeline complete with timestamps.
- [ ] Root cause and contributing factors identified.
- [ ] Action items assigned with owners and due dates.
- [ ] Vulnerability or security implications reviewed with SecOps if present.
- [ ] Postmortem reviewed by eng-sre and affected service owners.

C) Example incident timeline (abbreviated)
- 2026-01-10 08:12 UTC: Alert - 50% of requests returned 502 from model pool
- 08:15 UTC: Primary on-call acknowledged; IC assigned
- 08:22 UTC: Rolling restart of model runtime started
- 08:36 UTC: Partial restoration; status page posted
- 09:05 UTC: Full service restored; monitoring green
- 2026-01-12 12:00 UTC: Postmortem draft published
